q1: SELECT ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID FROM ACTORDIRECTOR GROUP BY ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID HAVING COUNT(*)>=3
q2: SELECT DISTINCT ACTOR_ID, DIRECTOR_ID FROM ACTORDIRECTOR AD GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING COUNT(*) >=3
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID FROM ACTORDIRECTOR GROUP BY ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID HAVING COUNT(*)>=3
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT ACTOR_ID, DIRECTOR_ID FROM ACTORDIRECTOR AD GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING COUNT(*) >=3
counterexample: INSERT INTO ACTORDIRECTOR (TIMESTAMP, ACTOR_ID, DIRECTOR_ID) VALUES (1, 101, 201), (2, 101, 201), (3, 102, 201);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 uses GROUP BY on all columns in the SELECT clause, while Q2 uses GROUP BY with column aliases (1 and 2) which can lead to different results if the order of columns in the SELECT clause changes.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have at least two rows with the same ACTOR_ID and DIRECTOR_ID, and the third row should have a different ACTOR_ID but the same DIRECTOR_ID as the first two rows. This will trigger the difference in results between Q1 and Q2.
